body:
@geoand cool, will give it a try!

But is spring-di even required for spring-data-jpa?
Not strictly, but in Spring proper you get it

I must say I'd really prefer to not have spring-di and I guess most other users would agree that are simply looking for a repository pattern data access solution (instead of an active record pattern like panache).
Would it be possible to remove that dependency or make it optional somehow? I know it could be a breaking change for some users but if the migration guide documents to add spring-di for those cases it should be ok.

PS: I would create a separate issue for that and would try to help where I can.
It's too big of a breaking change and there is no other extension we could use to make it a conditional dependency, so I'm going to leave it as is
I see. What about a kill switch for spring-di, effectively disabling the extension?
Sure, if you want to add some kind of build time property (and test it with the application you have in mind), I'd approve that.

issue.title: Add build-time property to disable `quarkus-spring-di`

labels.name: area/spring

issue.body:
### Description

As discussed [here (and the subsequent comments)](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/35011#issuecomment-1651260879), it can make sense to disable `quarkus-spring-di`, e.g. when you just want `spring-data-jpa` features without any spring injection support (which might increase the risk of issues/side effects, like #35011).
